source: សៀវភៅស្ដីពីដំណាំដំឡូងមី (Book on Cassava), Part 2, UNDP-supported capacity-building programme for cassava, March 2015
text:
Plant spacing: farmers plant cassava at varying spacing, generally ranging from about 50cm to 180cm between plants, with a planting density of roughly 10,000 to 25,000 plants per hectare able to give good yield. The best spacing for a given field depends on soil type and growing conditions.

Weed control: the source describes both mechanical inter-row weeding and chemical herbicide options, applied either pre-emergence or post-emergence:

Pre-emergence application (applied after planting, before weeds emerge, typically within 0-5 days of planting): example rates given are 1,500-2,250 g active ingredient/ha of metholachlor 50% EC, or 750-1,500 g active ingredient/ha of diuron 80% WP. This application is described as controlling weeds for approximately 30-45 days.

Post-emergence / inter-row application (applied later, once weeds and crop rows are established, directed at the row middles): example rates given are 500-750 g active ingredient/ha of paraquat 27.6% AS, or 1,500 g active ingredient/ha of glyphosate 48% AS.
caveat: Herbicide product names, formulation percentages, and application rates were cross-checked against a 300dpi high-resolution crop of the source page and are reported with reasonable confidence. As with any pesticide guidance, actual product labels and locally registered formulations should be checked before use, since registered products and rates can change over time and vary by location.
